Credits: Minecraft Uncensored library Imagine a world without the chains of censorship of authoritarian hold over press. And now, what if it does exist, hidden inside a video game we all see and talk about every day? Imagine a library. That’s easy. Now, imagine a library inside a video game. Still not that difficult. Now, imagine that the library is filled with books and articles that are banned in different countries. Imagine being able to access brilliant writings that often disappear under oppressive governments or due to differences in ideology. That’s exactly what the Uncensored Library does! Standing for our rights When a country’s ruling system becomes authoritarian in nature, even if not explicitly declared as such, one of the important sectors that takes a hit is journalism. Newspapers, magazines, websites and at times, even blogs get banned or controlled by such governments. Youngsters, in such situations, grow up in systems where opinions, views and information available are heavily censored, misinterpreted or distorted. left The Uncensored Library. Minecraft Uncensored Library Minecraft Uncensored Library https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/oz5x6f/article71619081.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/01_Uncensored_Library_Island.jpg minecraft The Uncensored Library (press kit). Credits: Minecraft Reporters Without Borders sought a way to overcome this challenge. In any country where the press is under stress and information is controlled, one thing they found is accessible to everyone were video games. In this case, Minecraft. This is where the idea of the Uncensored Library began. Minecraft, a block-based sandbox video game developed by Mojang Studios, is a video game where players explore, mine resources, craft tools, and build structures in a procedurally generated 3D world. The game does not have a fixed storyline or single required goal, making it similar to digital Lego. A library for all, by all After 24 builders and experts from 16 countries worked for 250 hours, the Uncensored Library was finally released on March 12, 2020, on World Day Against Cyber Censorship. The project was led by the Minecraft design studio BlockWorks in collaboration with Reporters Without Borders and used over 12.5 million Minecraft blocks to be created. left The Uncensored Library. Minecraft Uncensored Library Minecraft Uncensored Library https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/w3t8wa/article71619082.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/03_Uncensored_Library_front2.jpg minecraft Uncensored library With articles from multiple countries like Egypt, Belarus, Brazil, Eritrea, Iran, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam and the United States, the library currently consists of around 300 works and is growing. These articles, which are banned in several countries, are now available again within Minecraft, hidden from government surveillance technology. The books can be read by everyone on the server, but their content cannot be changed. Did you know? Created in neoclassical architectural style, the library has been built with inspiration taken from traditional Roman and Greek architecture. You might have noticed such design styles in many old museum or library buildings from around the world! How to access? The Uncensored library can be accessed through the game Minecraft: Java Edition. For this, you first need to install Minecraft: Java Edition and have a valid Minecraft account. Then to join the library, you first need to open the Minecraft launcher and select Minecraft: Java Edition. Please ensure that you are using Minecraft’s latest release (1.21.11) and press Play. left The Uncensored Library Minecraft Uncensored Library Minecraft Uncensored Library https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/acv2w5/article71619086.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/09_Uncensored_Library_US%20Room.jpg minecraft Uncensored library From the game’s main menu, select Multiplayer, and from the multiplayer menu, select Direct Connect. Finally, enter visit.uncensoredlibrary.com into the server address box and press Join Server. You will now be connected to the library!
